_blind_means: Given the pinned sha, the document and the artifact set it names, and nothing else. Did not read research/autonomy/ (other seat records, hardening state, receipts, ledger), and did not know what any other seat was doing or that other seats existed beyond the instruction that they review a different paper. Worked in its own worktree and branch. Told that finding nothing is a legitimate result, told to refute by default, and told to record UNKNOWN rather than write an identifier or statistic from recollection. One leak occurred and is disclosed below rather than used.
lens: Internal consistency. Took each load-bearing sentence and asked whether the artifact it cites supports it, contradicts it or is silent — abstract/headline against body, banner against sections, section against section, tier predicate against the tier's own verbatim criterion, and every printed statistic against the committed JSON that produces it. Re-derived part A (fusion calls, expression percentile, the Cellosaurus ST block), part B (both readable platforms' raw and proliferation-adjusted contrasts, the elevation cut, the probe-mapping and NCBI/UniGene diagnostics, the four-archive search counts), part C (all six genes' means, panel SDs, dependent fractions, Welch t, the coordination z and the axis mean/SD/delta), part D (every rho, t and n in both tables, the signed and absolute control means, both specificity bars, the proliferation bar and its margin), the structural census and construct designs, and §8's series metadata, identity check and the five preprint quotations. Also read emc_atr_vulnerability.py's grade() and part-B verdict logic directly, because a criterion is only as fixed as the code that applies it. Specifically probed the class-inheritance limit in both directions: whether it is asserted where the paper carries EMC-specific structural evidence, and whether it is quietly dropped anywhere.
what_i_read: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py (grading, part-B verdict, part-D GDSC residual construction)
research/manuscripts/program/emc-post-degrader-options.md (only to check the verbatim bound the headline quotes)
PubMed metadata for PMID 36316541 (one $0 fetch, to settle a year printed two ways)
central_claim: The published FET-fusion → impaired-ATM → compensatory-ATR-dependency hypothesis is tested for internal consistency in public data and for transfer to EMC, and the answer is graded WEAK on a scale fixed in advance: EMC tumours' DDR/replication-stress transcripts are elevated only as far as generic proliferation is (part B, two independent series), the CRISPR knockout readout is saturated and cannot discriminate even against a matched fusion-negative sarcoma comparator (part C), ATR-inhibitor sensitivity does not track the mechanism (part D, 1 of 4 pre-registered tests, and the one that passes is about the drug rather than about EMC), the DepMap line this repository called EMC is recorded by Cellosaurus as carrying no EWSR1 fusion (part A), and a 2026 sarcoma ATR programme from the best-fit collaborator selects on HRD rather than FET status (§8). The vulnerability itself is inherited from a class: it was measured on other FET fusions in other diseases, no NR4A3 fusion has been tested for it, and no efficacy, potency, dose, safety, window or readiness claim is made.

blockers.summary: ⛔ "No EMC line is in GDSC2" is FALSE against this document's own committed input cache, and it is printed twice — inside the ⛔ banner the document says is repeated in every artifact, and again in §6.2 item 2. The line DepMap labels EMC (ACH-001519 / H-EMC-SS) IS in GDSC2 8.5 and has residual LN_IC50 values for BOTH ATR inhibitors used in part D. The claim is load-bearing: it is the stated reason this assessment "cannot become that evidence at any sample size from any public dataset". The correct fact is already in the paper and is STRONGER — §2 establishes that this line is recorded as not carrying the fusion, so its ATR-inhibitor values are not a readout on an NR4A3 fusion — and a reader who checks the cache finds an unreported ATRi readout on the line the paper calls EMC sitting behind a sentence saying no such data exists.
blockers.evidence: Sentence, verbatim, at manuscript lines 40-41: "no ATR inhibitor has ever been put on an NR4A3-fusion-positive cell. No EMC line is in GDSC2; the one line DepMap labels EMC has no CRISPR data"; repeated at line 749. Refuted by research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability-inputs.json -> part_d.gdsc_residual_ln_ic50_by_drug: ACH-001519 is a key in ALL SEVEN drug maps — azd6738 (ceralasertib) residual -0.0047 in a 956-line map, ve-822 (berzosertib) +2.0477 in an 892-line map, plus paclitaxel -4.0902, olaparib +1.6678, talazoparib -0.7541, mk-1775 -0.87, bortezomib -7.8713. Those two map sizes are the same 956/892 the manuscript prints in §5. emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines ~2645-2676 build that map ONLY from rows of the GDSC2 fitted-dose-response table (gdsc_meta.source "GDSC2_8.5_27Oct23", n_rows 242036) whose SANGER_MODEL_ID/COSMIC_ID maps to a DepMap model, and the residual is LN_IC50 minus that line's own GDSC median — so a value cannot exist for a line absent from GDSC2. That ACH-001519 is the EMC-labelled line is the paper's own citation: research/modalities/fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> emc_line = {model_id ACH-001519, oncotree_label "Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma", has_crispr_gene_effect false}. Corroborated independently inside part A's own quoted record: emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_a_hemcss_identity.cellosaurus.record.DR carries "GDSC; 907290", "Cosmic-CLP; 907290", "Cell_Model_Passport; SIDM00535" and "Omics: Phenotyping; Drug screening". The CRISPR half of the same sentence IS correct (ACH-001519 is absent from part_d.atr_axis_dependency_by_line, 1178 lines). The charitable reading — that "EMC line" silently means "fusion-positive EMC line" — makes the clause circular with the sentence before it and still leaves the DepMap-labelled EMC line's GDSC2 ATRi values unreported.

p1s.summary: §6.1 asserts the fixed WEAK criterion is met "verbatim" and "precisely", and neither series satisfies it as written. On the series that actually carries the verdict, two UNRELATED control sets clear the same elevation cut — so it is not "only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes" that are elevated; on the second series NOTHING clears the cut, so it does not show generic elevation either. Row 1 of the same four-row table states the contradicting fact. This is the one section whose stated purpose is that the criteria cannot be softened after the fact, and the producing module's own `why` string carries the disjunct the prose drops.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript §6.1 predicate table row 4: "Only generic proliferation / DNA-damage genes are elevated | yes — which is the WEAK criterion, verbatim", and the paragraph below it: "The verbatim WEAK criterion is 'only generic proliferation/DNA-damage genes are elevated', and that is precisely what two independent EMC series show." Against emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature: unrelated_control_concepts_elevated = ["control_adipogenesis", "control_oxphos"], i.e. TWO sets that are neither proliferation nor DNA-damage clear §1's own >0.2 cut (pooled_raw_contrast: control_oxphos +0.3843 t 3.952, control_adipogenesis +0.2183 t 5.081 — oxphos is the LARGEST mover of any concept scored). The pooled read is GSE4303/GPL3290 alone (every pooled_raw_contrast entry has n_platforms 1; platforms_with_a_readable_EMC_vs_comparator_contrast lists that one file; series_carrying_the_verdict "GSE4303"). On the concordance series the same cut is cleared by nothing at all: per_platform["GSE24369_series_matrix.txt.gz"].contrast_EMC_vs_all_comparator_sarcoma has proliferation_MYC +0.0844, control_oxphos +0.1131, every DDR concept |delta| <= 0.0445. §3.4 states the contradicting fact plainly ("the two unrelated control sets (oxphos, adipogenesis) move as much as or more than any DDR set"), as does §6.1's own row 1. The artifact's grading.why keeps the qualifier the prose loses: "… the DDR concepts do not survive adjustment for proliferation, OR unrelated control sets move with them", and emc_atr_vulnerability.py computes the predicate as `bool(sig_present and sig_specific is False)`, not from the criterion's words. The tier itself is not disputed — WEAK is the closest of the three and the module's own output — only the claim that the criterion is met verbatim.

p1s.summary: §1 says "A fourth outcome exists and is not in the fixed list, so it is named rather than folded into one of the three: NOT_ASSESSABLE." The producing module carries a FIFTH outcome outside the fixed list — MODERATE_PLUS — which the manuscript never names anywhere. The enumeration is the point of that paragraph: it is what tells a reader the outcome space was fixed in advance and is completely disclosed.
p1s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py, grade(): the tier branches are STRONG, WEAK, MODERATE, MODERATE_PLUS and NOT_ASSESSABLE. MODERATE_PLUS's own why string is "The signature holds and one of the two surrogate mechanism tests supports it, but not both, so the STRONG conjunction is not met. Reported between the fixed tiers rather than rounded up to STRONG." `grep -n MODERATE` over the pinned manuscript returns exactly one line — line 154, the verbatim MODERATE criterion — and no occurrence of MODERATE_PLUS. Its omission does not flatter the result (MODERATE_PLUS is a refusal to round up), which is why this is a disclosure defect rather than a grading one.

p1s.summary: §6.1 uses part C as one of three sides of a bound, which §4 forbids in terms. §4 ends "it must not be quoted as evidence against the hypothesis … This readout can support the hypothesis or miss it. It cannot refute it"; §6.1 then writes "a bound on three sides now instead of two: no coordinated dependency, no sensitivity tracking ATM status, and no proliferation-independent DDR signature". A blind instrument's null is an absent reading, and counting it as a bound is the exact collapse §1 built the NOT_ASSESSABLE tier to refuse — applied to part B and not to part C.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript §4 closing paragraph vs §6.1 paragraph 2. emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_c_coordinated_dependency.verdict "INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND", verdict_reading "… this instrument cannot support OR refute a selective ATR-axis dependency in FET-fusion lines. Reported as a failed instrument", and knockout_instrument_with_matched_comparator._criterion defines blindness as the axis sitting at the common-essential floor with the between-group delta smaller than the within-group SD (axis_mean_sarcoma_pool -1.34, axis_sd_sarcoma_pool 0.1904, delta_FET_minus_matched -0.0065, frac_lines_dependent_on_axis_sarcoma_pool 1.0). The same section's predicate row also answers "Other FET-fusion models show selective ATR-pathway dependency" with "no — instrument blind (§4)"; that rendering is defensible for a predicate meaning 'was it shown', but the prose then converts it into an evidential bound, which is not.

p1s.summary: The headline calls the one passing mechanism test "two instruments agreeing about the same target"; §5 says in terms that the agreement is at MODULE level rather than at target level, that the predictor is a three-gene mean, and that nothing in the analysis separates ATR from a neighbouring checkpoint kinase. The correction landed in §5 and not in the summary that a reader takes away — the one-of-a-pair shape this document's own Appendix records three times.
p1s.evidence: Headline: "the one that passes is a statement about the drug rather than about EMC (lines more ATR-dependent by CRISPR are more ATR-inhibitor-sensitive — two instruments agreeing about the same target)". §5: "This is an internal-consistency check passing, at MODULE level rather than at target level", "no bar in this analysis separates ATR from a neighbouring checkpoint kinase". The predictor is emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity["dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect"] — a mean gene effect over three genes, not one target — and its per_drug_rho_near_neighbour_DDR records mk-1775 (WEE1i) at rho +0.1571 (t 3.893, n 601) against berzosertib's +0.1726 (t 4.157, n 565), with no interval computed for either.

p1s.summary: The headline's "what still stands" table sources the two-fusion RG bracket to emc_fet_idr_census.py, and that artifact contains only ONE EMC fusion, labels it `emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3`, and runs its whole comparative verdict on that label — the exact drift the Appendix says was flagged on 2026-08-03 and corrected. The prose is right and the census pointer is stale: the type-1 numbers the row prints exist only in the sibling construct-designs artifact, and the census's headline claim is true of type 2 and false of the fusion the paper calls EMC's actual commonest.
p1s.evidence: Manuscript headline table row 1 cites "emc_fet_idr_census.py and emc_fet_construct_designs.py" for "type 2 … EWSR1(1-264) … 0 of 30; type 1 (EWSR1 exon 12::NR4A3 exon 3, the actual commonest EMC fusion) retains EWSR1(1-431) and keeps 8 of 30". emc-fet-idr-census.json holds exactly one EMC record, `emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3` = {last_fet_residue_retained 264, rg_dipeptides_retained 0, fraction_of_wildtype_RG_retained 0.0, breakpoint_provenance "EWSR1 transcript exon 7"}; the string "431" does not occur anywhere in the file (grep -c = 0). Its emc_vs_measured_fusions_comparative._claim_under_test is "EMC's canonical fusion loses at least as much of EWSR1's RGG content as each fusion in which ATM suppression was MEASURED" with holds_against_every_measured_type true — true at 0.0 for type 2, false for type 1 at 0.267 against EWSR1::FLI1 (0.0) and EWSR1::ATF1 e8 (0.233). The type-1 figures ARE sourced: emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> constructs[0].junction_in_residue_numbering.five_prime_residues_fully_encoded = 431 and rgg_dose_calibration_and_predictions.emc_constructs_on_the_same_axis type 1 = {rg_dipeptides_retained 8, fraction 0.267}. The Appendix's own standing lesson applies to the copy that remains: "A correction is not applied until every copy has been searched for by string."

p2s.summary: §4's one-line justification for INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND reads as the reverse of the sentence it follows: "A readout on which essentially nothing is negative cannot discriminate", immediately after "99.2-100 % of lines 'dependent'" and a table of gene effects between -0.71 and -2.74. On the numeric reading of 'negative' (DepMap gene effect; the module's own dependent_threshold is -0.5) essentially EVERYTHING is negative, which is the actual argument. Recoverable from context, and the artifact states the criterion correctly, but the sentence as printed inverts it.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript §4 paragraph after the gene table. emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_c_coordinated_dependency.knockout_instrument_with_matched_comparator._criterion: "the knockout readout is BLIND on this axis when (a) the axis sits at or below the common-essential floor (~ -1) panel-wide, and (b) the between-group delta is smaller than the within-group SD", with frac_lines_dependent_on_axis_sarcoma_pool 1.0 and dependent_threshold -0.5.

p2s.summary: GSE299349's deposit date is printed two ways. §3.0a calls it "deposited 2026-06-04"; §8.1 records "submitted Jun 09 2025, released Jun 04 2026". The only artifact evidence is a submission_date of Jun 09 2025 and a last_update_date of Jun 04 2026 — there is no release-date field, and 2026-06-04 is not a deposit date under either reading.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript §3.0a ("68 samples, deposited 2026-06-04") vs §8.1 provenance row. atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> series_record.submission_date "Jun 09 2025", last_update_date "Jun 04 2026". Neither date string occurs anywhere in emc-atr-vulnerability.json or its inputs cache, so §3.0a's date is not carried by the part-B search record it sits in.

p2s.summary: The Bangerter citation is printed with two different years for one PMID: §2.2 says Hum Cell 2023;36:446-455 and the Appendix says Hum Cell 2022;36:446-455. The quoted sentence itself is verbatim correct and the bound drawn from it (<10 % fusion-negative, and no further) is sound; only the year disagrees with itself.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript line 247 vs line 1028, both PMID 36316541. According to PubMed the record's publication_date is 2022-11-01, journal Hum Cell, volume 36 issue 1 pages 446-455, DOI 10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x (https://doi.org/10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x), and its abstract carries the quoted clause "EMCs are translocation sarcomas and harbor in > 90% of the cases an NR4A3 rearrangement" verbatim. The paper's own part_a_hemcss_identity.literature record carries year "2023" for the same PMID (Europe PMC's issue year), which is presumably where the live text's 2023 came from — so the two copies are each traceable, and they still disagree in print.

p2s.summary: §3.1's enumeration does not sum to the total it states: five samples are missing from a sentence that reads as exhaustive ("Reading all seven: …").
p2s.evidence: Manuscript §3.1: "10 EMC tumours sit together on GPL3290, beside 3 GIST and 3 DFSP on the same print run, with 4 MFH/UPS on GPL3254 and 2 more GIST on GPL3335 — 27 classified samples in total" enumerates 22. The 27 is right: emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature.series_readability.GSE4303.class_counts = {EMC 10, GIST 5, DFSP 8, MFH_UPS 4, unclassified 9}. The five unmentioned samples are DFSP on two further platforms — per_platform GSE4303-GPL3288 {DFSP 2, unclassified 1} and GSE4303-GPL3289 {DFSP 3}.

p2s.summary: The banner calls the structural census "The one EMC-specific strand", while the headline table lists four EMC-specific structural items that survive parts C and D, at least one of which (placing EMC's fusions on the source authors' own measured RGG dose curve) is a second sequence-derived argument bearing on transfer rather than a downstream design artifact. A count, not a direction: the class-inheritance limit itself holds everywhere I could test it.
p2s.evidence: Banner: "The one EMC-specific strand does not close that gap, and saying which strand it is matters" (naming the census). Headline: "Four things in this programme's ATR arm are structural arguments from sequence" — census, construct designs, RGG dose-calibration prediction, TCF12 within-EMC control. emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> rgg_dose_calibration_and_predictions places all four EMC constructs on the source's own measured anchors (source_anchors, measured_comparator_fusions, emc_constructs_on_the_same_axis), i.e. it is an EMC-specific structural placement and not merely a proposal.

p2s.summary: §5's "building one needs a drug set this analysis does not have" overstates by one clause. The module does compute a target-vs-adjacent-target comparison for every predictor; what it does not have is a BAR, which the same paragraph says correctly two clauses earlier and which the artifact states in terms.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript §5: "Every specificity bar here is DDR-vs-not or drug-vs-general-sensitivity; none is target-vs-adjacent-target, and building one needs a drug set this analysis does not have." emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity carries mean_rho_across_near_neighbour_DDR and per_drug_rho_near_neighbour_DDR (mk-1775) for all nine predictors, and _two_specificity_axes says "mean_rho_across_near_neighbour_DDR … REPORTING ONLY: no bar, no test and no `passes` value reads any of them" — so the 'no bar' half is exactly right and the 'no drug set' half is not. The paper itself prints the mk-1775 row.

p2s.summary: §8.4 states how the published paper's analysis treated the EMC sample — "with the EMC model outside the biomarker analysis" — in a document that twice says that paper's full text was never read. The deposit supports the weaker, sufficient statement (the six cell models are outside the series' STATED DESIGN), and the abstract the paper quotes says the authors pharmacotyped patient-derived cell models, so the EMC model was in some analysis.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript §8.4 point 3 vs §8.1 ("not open access, so only the abstract was read") and §8.5 item 4 ("its full text is paywalled"). atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json -> design_vs_contents = {n_samples_actually_in_the_series 68, n_samples_the_design_accounts_for 62, overall_design_verbatim …}; q3_selection_biomarker.n_samples_with_an_HRD_term = 0, so no deposited field says which samples entered the SARC-HRD analysis. §8.5 item 5 draws exactly this distinction for a neighbouring claim ("Not addressing an idea and rejecting it are different, and only the first is observed").

p2s.summary: One statistic is printed with two different roundings across the two documents that share it: paclitaxel's line-median-corrected delta is -0.526 here and -0.525 in the source this headline imports from. Cosmetic, and both are roundings of the same artifact value.
p2s.evidence: Manuscript headline ("Delta -0.526, t -3.08") against research/manuscripts/program/emc-post-degrader-options.md line 398 ("-0.525 (-3.08)"). fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> atr_inhibitor_sensitivity_gdsc.by_drug.paclitaxel.welch_line_median_corrected.delta_a_minus_b = -0.5255, t -3.076. The verbatim bound the headline quotes from that file ("it does not isolate ATR, and it must not be written as if it did") IS present at its line 413 and is quoted accurately.

leaks: Yes, two, both disclosed rather than discarded, and neither used. FIRST: a repo-wide `git grep -n "isolate ATR" <pin>` — run to verify that the headline's quoted bound really is verbatim in emc-post-degrader-options.md — returned two research/autonomy paths in its output: research/autonomy/hardening-state/PUB-ATR.json and one earlier seat record for a DIFFERENT commit (0448a27a…), each printing one long evidence string about the paclitaxel/ATR-isolation issue at that earlier commit. The seat did not open either file and ran no further repo-wide grep. Nothing above rests on those lines: every finding in this record was reached before that command from the manuscript and the modality artifacts, and the issue those lines describe is already fixed at this pin (the headline now names paclitaxel, prints its delta and quotes the bound), so it is not reported here. SECOND, and unavoidable: writing this record made gate 3 (`emc_systems_map_check.py`, rule O4) red, because a tracked file naming ACH-001519 must be classified in OBJ-LINE-HEMCSS's `read_by`. Clearing it required reading that block of research/manuscripts/emc-systems-map.json, which lists earlier seat records for this and other papers BY FILENAME and carries one `why_unaffected` string summarising a round-3 regression-seat blocker (§2.3 read as a stale present-tense survey). The seat opened no seat record, and reports nothing on §2.3 — at this pin that section is re-verified 2026-09-02 with all eight rows closed, so the earlier finding is already fixed and was not re-reported. The same pass appended this record's own `unaffected` classification to that list, which is the only registry edit the seat made. Separately, CLAUDE.md was injected into the seat's context by the harness before its first command rather than read by any command of its own.
_logs_are_not_durable: The seat's logs live in the session scratchpad, which dies with the container. The findings above are its report as delivered; every one names the manuscript location and the artifact path and field that reproduces it, so none depends on a log surviving.
